title: Partial oral antibiotic treatment for bacterial brain abscess: An open-label randomised non-inferiority trial (ORAL)
official: Partial oral antibiotic treatment for bacterial brain abscess: An open-label randomised non-inferiority trial (ORAL)
summary: Main objective: To determine whether oral antibiotics are non-inferior (margin 10%) to IV antibiotics for bacterial brain abscess assessed by numbers meeting a primary, objective endpoint at 6 months after randomisation

interventions.name: Moxifloxacin Tillomed 400 mg film coated tablets
CEFTRIAXONE ARROW 1 g/3,5 ml, poudre et solvant pour solution injectable (IM)
Meropenem 2 g powder for solution for injection/infusion

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Age >17 years
2. Clinical presentation and brain imaging consistent with brain abscess
3. The physician in charge decides to treat the patient for brain abscess
4. Able to absorb oral medications
5. To have received guideline recommended intravenous antimicrobials for at least 14 consecutive days or longer before randomisation and no additional aspiraiton or excision of brain abscess planned.
6. Expected to be treated for at least another 14 days after randomisation.
7. No progression in neurological deficits or new-onset neurological symptoms (excluding seizures) within 5 days before randomisation
Exclusion criteria:
1. Hypersensitivity to the intended antimicrobial with no other alternative drugs available
2. Patients not capable of providing informed consent.
3. Expected substantially reduced compliance with treatment
4. Pregnancy (confirmed by urine or plasma human chorionic gonadotropin test in fertile women)
5. Lactating women
6. Concomitant treatment for proven or suspected CNS infection caused by mycobacteria, nocardia spp., pseudomonas spp., fungi, toxoplasmosis, or other CNS parasites
7. Device related brain abscesses (e.g. deep brain stimulators, ventriculo-peritoneal shunts)
8. Severe immuno-compromise defined as uncontrolled HIV/AIDS (see Glossary), acute myeloid leukaemia, acute lymphoblastic leukaemia, haematological stem-cell transplant recipients, and organ transplant recipients. For patients with other types of haematological conditions (see Glossary) or with an ongoing need for biological- or chemotherapy, prednisolone >20 mg/day for ≥14 days, opportunistic pathogens listed under exclusion criterion #5 should be excluded as the cause of the bacterial brain abscess.
9. Concomitant or unrelated infections requiring >7 days of intravenous antimicrobials
10. Previous enrolment into this trial
